haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes only to the shadow store, never charging or writing the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine computes, writes the ledger, and charges. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store only, so it stays current.
haiku-low.q3: Gate A: 7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1%, and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person asks to advance; the controller checks the record and refuses if unmet.
haiku-low.q4: The controller starts rollback itself when charge failure rate exceeds 2% in any 10-minute window. This happens in both or new_only, not shadow.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only via RB_Handover. Before the new engine can return, the rollout must go through shadow again, and the 7- and 14-day counts restart from zero.
haiku-low.q6: Rollback from new_only is possible only before day 35 after entering new_only. Later, usage events the old engine skipped are gone and cannot be replayed.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read the billing_mode flag to pick an engine. How quickly they notice a change is NOT STATED. Before every charge they read the charge hold, which stops them while set.
haiku-low.q8: In a durable rollout record next to the ledger, written by the controller. The controller checks the gate from that record and refuses the forward move if unmet.
haiku-low.q9: The rollback controller measures charge failure rate across any 10-minute window. When it exceeds 2%, it starts the rollback itself and on-call is notified.
haiku-low.q10: The charge hold stops all charging, so due charges go into the queue under idempotency keys, held not dropped. They are charged late by the old engine at RB_Handover.
haiku-low.q11: The idempotency key (customer, billing period): the ledger is checked before charging and the provider rejects repeats. Unknown outcomes are looked up at the provider first.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays in that step with the hold still set and due charges queued; the flag is unchanged. The step is retried and on-call paged; restart resumes from the recorded step.

sonnet.q1: The old engine computes, writes the ledger and charges. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes to the shadow store only. It never charges and never writes the ledger.
sonnet.q2: The new engine computes, writes the ledger and charges. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store only, so it stays current.
sonnet.q3: Gate A must be met: 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1%, and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person asks the rollout controller to advance. The controller checks the gate and sets the flag.
sonnet.q4: The controller watches charge outcomes. It starts a rollback itself when the charge failure rate is over 2% in any 10-minute window. This applies in both and new_only, and in new_only only before day 35.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only, with the gates reset. The 7-day and 14-day counts restart from zero, and the rollout must go through shadow again.
sonnet.q6: It stops at day 35 or later, counted from entering new_only. After that the usage events the old engine skipped are gone and cannot be replayed. Decommissioning also ends rollback.
sonnet.q7: Workers follow the billing_mode flag in the config service. NOT STATED how they find out about a change (how quickly they notice is listed as unknown). For a switch, the charge hold is set first and in-flight charge calls finish or time out. Workers read the hold before every charge. NOT STATED for invoice computation in progress.
sonnet.q8: The evidence is in the rollout record: gate counters, daily comparison results and Finance sign-off. The controller checks the gate from the record and refuses to advance if it is not met.
sonnet.q9: The rollout controller. It measures the charge failure rate, which must be over 2% in any 10-minute window. When that is met it starts the rollback itself and notifies on-call.
sonnet.q10: Due charges are put in the charge queue under their idempotency keys. They are held, not dropped. They are charged by the old engine after RB_Handover, once the flag is set to old_only and the hold is cleared. The old engine charges those that are due and not yet in the ledger.
sonnet.q11: The idempotency key (customer, billing period). The ledger is checked before any charge and the provider rejects a repeat. RB_Reconcile also matches every charge between ledger and provider, and adds a ledger entry if the provider shows one the ledger lacks. Only (customer, billing period) pairs not in the ledger get charged.
sonnet.q12: The rollback stays in the failed step (RB_Reconcile or RB_Reprocess), retries and pages on-call. The hold stays set, due charges stay queued, and the flag is not changed until RB_Handover. After a controller restart it resumes from the recorded step, and each step is safe to repeat.
